전부 날짜순으로 정리돼 있었음

첫 영화표, 첫 커피, 첫 회

버린 줄 알았는데 남친이 받아서 넣어둔 거였음

"카드로 내면 기록이 숫자로만 남잖아"

This man dedicated his life to hauling thousands of gallons of water to wildlife dying of thirst — and continued directing the mission from his hospital bed until his final days.

He was only 54 when he died.

In 2016, a devastating drought turned Kenya’s Tsavo West National Park into a parched wasteland. Horrified by the sight of a buffalo collapsing from thirst, local pea farmer Patrick Kilonzo Mwalua sold his possessions, bought a secondhand truck, and began delivering up to 3,000 gallons of water every day to desperate elephants, zebras, and antelope across the rugged terrain.

His selfless work, captured in viral videos of thirsty animals rushing toward his truck, turned him into an international symbol of compassion. People from Vermont to Utah rallied behind the man known as the “Water Man of Tsavo,” donating generously to keep the lifeline flowing when rains failed.

Even as kidney failure took a heavy toll on his health, Mwalua refused to stop. From his hospital bed, he continued managing operations, coordinating daily deliveries, and developing new solutions such as solar-powered pumps and beehive fences to protect both wildlife and local communities.

Though he ultimately lost his battle with illness, his wife Rachel and the Mwalua Wildlife Trust carry on his work today.

Patrick Kilonzo Mwalua’s legacy is a powerful reminder that while we cannot prevent every tragedy, there is deep dignity and meaning in choosing kindness and action in the face of suffering.

For decades, people living with fibromyalgia were told their pain was purely psychological, yet a massive genetic study of 2.5 million people confirms the condition is rooted in the nervous system.

An international research team, including scientists from King's College London, the University of Toronto, and Fred Hutch Cancer Center, pooled genetic data from more than 2.5 million adults across 11 cohorts in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Northern Europe, including roughly 55,000 individuals diagnosed with fibromyalgia. By scanning millions of genetic markers across the genome, the researchers identified 26 distinct DNA regions linked to a higher risk of developing the disorder, with the implicated genes heavily concentrated in brain and nerve cell function.

The strongest genetic signal appeared in HTT, the same gene responsible for Huntington's disease when it carries a different mutation, and overall genetic risk was found exclusively in brain tissue and neural cells. The findings were published in the peer-reviewed journal Nature Medicine.

Affecting roughly 2% of the global population, fibromyalgia causes widespread chronic pain, severe fatigue, disrupted sleep, and memory difficulties, yet countless patients have historically had their symptoms dismissed as being "all in their heads". These new results reinforce the understanding that fibromyalgia stems from how the central nervous system processes pain signals. The analysis also revealed strong genetic overlap with low back pain, irritable bowel syndrome, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), helping explain why these conditions frequently occur together.

Still, the researchers emphasize that the discovery does not immediately yield a genetic diagnostic test or a new medication, and genetics alone do not determine who develops fibromyalgia, since environmental or physical triggers such as an arthritic injury may also be required. Even so, because one of the biological pathways uncovered in the study is already being targeted in clinical trials for Huntington's disease, researchers hope the overlap could give future fibromyalgia drug development a valuable head start.

[Kerrebijn, I., et al. (2026). The genetic architecture of fibromyalgia across 2.5 million individuals. Nature Medicine. (Published July 28, 2026; DOI: 10.1038/s41591-026-04492-6)]

A Pennsylvania teenager who dedicated her short life to serving others could eventually become the Catholic Church's first Generation Z saint.

Maria Middleton passed away from brain cancer in 2020 at the age of 18. On November 17, 2026, U.S. Catholic bishops voted during their annual fall assembly to support advancing her cause for beatification and canonization at the diocesan level.

Born in Doylestown, Pennsylvania, in 2002, Maria began volunteering and organizing charity efforts long before she became ill. As a child, she helped run coat drives and spent Thanksgiving holidays distributing donations to families in Harlem. In high school, she organized a fundraiser for children with cancer and their families, even before receiving her own diagnosis, while also preparing meals for older adults and collecting gifts for children in need.

During her sophomore year of high school, doctors discovered an inoperable brain tumor. As her illness progressed, she endured blurred vision, severe headaches, balance difficulties, and declining fine motor skills. Despite those physical challenges, she traveled to Uganda on a mission trip nine months after her diagnosis and continued raising funds to improve the school she visited even after returning home.

Her dedication to service and deep Catholic faith form the core of the case now under consideration by Church authorities. However, the bishops' vote represents an early procedural milestone rather than a final declaration. It signals formal support for a local diocesan investigation into her life, virtues, and writings, but it does not declare her a saint or guarantee canonization.

In the Catholic Church, the path to sainthood requires a thorough investigation, and for a non-martyr, beatification and canonization ordinarily require the formal Vatican verification of two miracles attributed to the candidate's intercession. Maria joins a small group of young candidates whose causes could one day result in the first canonized Gen Z saint, though there is no set timeline for when that process might conclude.

[United States Conference of Catholic Bishops (USCCB) & Archdiocese of Philadelphia. (2026, November 17). U.S. Bishops Affirm Advancement of the Cause of Beatification and Canonization of Servant of God Maria Middleton (Fall Plenary Assembly Action, Baltimore, MD)]

AI data centers may be an even bigger financial disaster than previously estimated, as the specialized chips and facilities powering the artificial intelligence boom become obsolete so quickly that the underlying economics might never work, according to a hedge fund founder.

Harris Kupperman, founder of the hedge fund Praetorian Capital, initially published an essay arguing that AI data centers had an impossibly narrow window to generate a return on investment. After industry insiders flooded his inbox with messages, further conversations led him to conclude that his original assumptions had actually been far too generous.

While Kupperman had initially assumed the computing hardware inside a facility would remain useful for roughly 10 years, data center insiders told him that the physical facilities themselves last only three to ten years at most, largely because AI hardware evolves at a breakneck pace and the chips run continuously at full capacity.

"No one understands how the financial math is supposed to work," Kupperman wrote. "They are as baffled as I am, and they do this for a living." By his calculations, the industry required between $320 billion and $480 billion in annual revenue simply to break even on a single year of capital spending, whereas actual end-user AI revenue was closer to $20 billion per year.

Factoring in the following year's wave of new data center construction pushes his estimated break-even threshold to roughly $1 trillion. "If the economics don't work, doing it at massive scale doesn't make the economics work any better," he warned. "It just takes an industry crisis and makes it into a national economic crisis."

Still, several important caveats apply. These estimates represent one investor's back-of-the-envelope calculations based on industry conversations rather than audited corporate financial filings. Moreover, Kupperman published the analysis in the fall of 2025, meaning AI revenues have expanded since then, and major technology companies strongly push back against claims of an AI infrastructure bubble. Even so, as massive data center projects continue driving up electricity costs and corporate debt, his central question about who ultimately foots the bill is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.

[Kupperman, H. (2025, September 2). Global Crossing Reborn... (Part II) [Blog essay & industry analysis]. Praetorian Capital / Kuppy's Event-Driven Monitor]

The tropical Pacific Ocean is currently hotter than at any point in recorded history.

El Niño is a naturally occurring climate pattern in which a massive pool of unusually warm water spreads across the equatorial Pacific, and scientists gauge its intensity by measuring how much warmer than normal sea surface temperatures are in a key monitoring zone of the central Pacific. In September, daily anomalies in that region surged to 3.11°C above average, shattering the previous daily record set in 2015, while September as a whole registered as the warmest month there since instrumental records began in the mid-1800s.

After evaluating 656 forecast runs across 14 climate models, climate analysis outlet Carbon Brief projects that this event is on track to peak around 4°C above normal in December, more than a full degree higher than any prior record. Climate scientist Zeke Hausfather described the surge as "simply staggering," noting that it "may end up being the strongest El Niño event in the past millennium."

Because El Niño alters where the ocean releases heat into the atmosphere, it reshuffles weather systems worldwide. The ongoing event has already helped fuel devastating wildfires in Indonesia and powerful typhoons across the western Pacific, and because global surface temperatures typically lag behind Pacific warming by several months, Carbon Brief estimates a 96% probability that 2027 will become Earth's hottest year on record.

Still, scientists note several important caveats. No forecast model has ever been tested against an El Niño of this magnitude, and several models ran slightly warm earlier in the year, leaving the exact December peak uncertain. Furthermore, the thousand-year comparison relies on paleoclimate reconstructions from natural archives such as coral reefs rather than direct thermometer measurements. Even so, the coming weeks will reveal just how intense this super El Niño becomes and how dramatically it reshapes global weather patterns.

[Climate Analysis Report: Hausfather, Z. (2026, November 6). 'Simply staggering': Rapidly developing 'super El Niño' on track to peak in December (Data analysis of 656 model runs across 14 climate models). Carbon Brief]

Europe's largest owl species has just put a £2 billion AI data center project on hold in Norway.

British developer GreenScale, backed by more than £1 billion in funding from German investment firm DTCP, had planned to build the Tonstad Datapark in Sirdal, a hydropower-rich municipality in southern Norway. Although local officials initially supported the development, the region's state administrator has now revoked the project's planning approval, ruling that it was waved through without a comprehensive planning process or proper environmental impact assessments.

Local residents had raised concerns over noise, heavy power consumption, and excess heat from the facility, while environmental groups argued that authorities failed to properly evaluate the impact on nearby wildlife, particularly the Eurasian eagle owl. Known locally in Norway as the hubro, Europe's largest owl is classified as an endangered species in the country, and formal complaints noted that the birds had been recorded in the area.

The ruling arrives amid a broader European backlash against rapid data center expansion, including protests held earlier this month under the banner of Stop Dirty Data Centres. It also serves as a pointed reminder that the AI boom depends heavily on vast tracts of land, abundant electricity, and quiet rural locations, which frequently overlap with sensitive wildlife habitats.

Still, the project is not necessarily finished. An independent three-week bird survey submitted in March 2025 detected no Eurasian eagle owl activity on the site, local politicians maintain that regional biodiversity will not be significantly harmed, and GreenScale states that it remains fully committed to the campus and will comply with all required regulatory procedures. Sirdal's municipality must now decide whether to pursue a fresh approval process, a move that could delay construction for months while ensuring the owls finally receive a thorough environmental review.

[Regulatory Ruling & News Reporting: State Administrator in Agder (Statsforvalteren i Agder) Planning Revocation Decision for Tonstad DataPark, Sirdal Municipality (November 2026); reported via E24 & The Telegraph (November 10–23, 2026)]

내가 밥을 먹은 날마다 동그라미가 하나씩 있었음
3년에 214개였음
마지막 장에는 내 이름이 적혀 있었음
그 아래에 할머니 글씨로 한 줄이 있었음
"우리 딸도, 한국에서 밥은 거르지 않았으면"

할머니 딸은 30년 전에 한국으로 시집갔음
처음 몇 년은 편지가 왔는데, 어느 날부터 끊겼음
할머니는 딸이 한국 어디에서 사는지 모른다고 했음
"한국 젊은 애가 밥 먹는 거 보면, 우리 딸도 저렇게 먹고 있겠지 싶어서"
그래서 돈을 못 받았다고 했음
밥값을 받는 게 아니라, 안부를 확인하는 거였음

내가 수첩을 돌려주자 할머니가 고개를 저었음
"가져가. 한국 가서, 혹시라도 만나면 전해 줘"
"잘 먹고 있다고, 엄마가 봤다고"

귀국하고 5년이 지났음
나는 아직 할머니 딸을 못 만났음
대신 매년 오사카에 갔음
가게는 그대로고, 할머니는 아직도 내 돈을 안 받으려고 했음
작년부터는 내가 먼저 계산대에 돈을 올려두고 도망 나왔음

수첩은 지금 내 책상 서랍에 있음
동그라미는 214개에서 멈춰 있음
한국 어딘가에, 이 수첩의 마지막 장을 읽어야 할 사람이 있음

오사카에서 3년 유학했음
학교 앞에 의자 8개짜리 작은 식당이 있었음
할머니 혼자 하는 가게였음
학생 정식은 500엔이었음

근데 나는 3년 동안 그 가게에서 돈을 낸 적이 거의 없었음
할머니는 항상 이유를 만들었음
"오늘은 재료가 남았어"
"새 메뉴니까 맛 평가해 줘"
"계산기는 고장 났어"
옆자리 일본 학생들은 전부 돈을 냈음
나한테만 공짜였음

처음엔 한국인이라 미안해서 그런 줄 알았음
두 번째 해에는 일부러 돈을 카운터에 올려두고 나왔음
다음 날 가면 그 돈이 내 자리에 그대로 놓여 있었음
할머니는 모르는 척했음

졸업하고 귀국하는 전날, 마지막으로 갔음
그날은 내가 먼저 말했음
"오늘은 꼭 낼게요. 3년 치 다는 못 내도, 오늘 거라도요"
할머니가 처음으로 웃지 않았음
카운터 서랍을 열더니, 낡은 수첩 한 권을 꺼냈음

   불편하거나 아픈 상태에서 벗어나는 순간의 희열
   (직전에 느꼈던 고통 때문에 평범한 상태도 즐겁게 느껴짐)

4. 갑작스러운 영광
   남이 넘어지거나 실수하는 모습을 보고 웃는 것
   (상대적으로 내가 더 나아 보이는 순간의 우월감)

5. 심리적 마조히즘
   질투나 상실감 같은 정신적 고통을 즐기는 것
   (자신의 것을 빼앗기거나 상처받는 상황에서 오히려 흥분과 쾌감을 느낌)

6. 통제권 상실의 쾌감
   자신의 의지와 상관없이 상황이 흘러가는 것을 즐기는 것
   (스스로 통제할 수 없는 상황과 무력감에서 오히려 해방감이나 흥분을 느낌)

7. 알아보는 쾌감
   징그러운 벌레도 잘 그린 그림으로 보면 즐거운 것
   (대상을 알아보고 이해하는 것 자체에서 즐거움을 느낌)

8. 아무것도 하지 않는 쾌감
   물멍이나 불멍을 하면서 시간을 보내는 것
   (생각과 걱정을 멈추고 그저 존재하는 것만으로 행복을 느낌)

9. 물에서 보는 폭풍
   안전한 곳에서 위험한 상황을 지켜보는 것
   (남의 불행이 즐거운 게 아니라 내가 그 불행을 겪지 않는다는 안도감)

10. 젠주흐트
    노을이나 풍경을 보면서 알 수 없는 그리움을 느끼는 것
    (무언가를 갈망하고 그 채워지지 않는 감정 자체를 즐김)

다른 건 모르겠고 3번은 격하게 공감됨
힐 신고 하루 종일 걸어다니다가 집에 와서 벗는 순간의 쾌감은 진짜 ㅇㅈ 발가락 10개가 동시에 해방되는 기분임

「この写真、私が撮ったのよ。コンテストに出すから、あなたのは消して」

市民公園の紅葉撮影会、池のほとりの休憩所で開かれた講評の時間に、同じ班の女性にそう言われた。

しかもその写真は、裏に女性の名前を書かれて、もう講師の先生の前の「提出」の箱に入っていた。

撮影会は市の写真連盟が毎年11月に開いていて、参加費は1,500円。

最後に一人1枚だけプリントして、先生に講評してもらえる。

いい写真は、連盟の推薦で市のフォトコンテストに出してもらえる。

女性は、朝の集合のときから私の隣にいた、柴田さんという人だった。

柴田さん「あなた、三脚なんか持ってきたの？ 重いだけよ。三脚に頼るのは素人」

柴田さん「私は15年、手持ち一本。ブレないのが腕なの」

私は入門機と、中古で買った三脚で、朝の日を背中に受けながら、池の太鼓橋を撮った。

風がやんだ一瞬、水面に紅葉と橋がそのまま映って、そこに白いサギが降りてきた。

1枚だけ、撮れた。

休憩所の受付で、小型プリンターから写真が出てくるのを待っていたら、後ろから柴田さんの手が伸びた。

柴田さん「あら、これ私のね」

私「いえ、それは私が今出した分です」

柴田さん「同じ場所で撮ったんだから、同じに見えるのは当たり前でしょ。私のよ」

柴田さんはその場で、写真の裏にボールペンで自分の名前を書いた。

そして提出の箱に入れた。

私「待ってください。私のカメラにデータがあります」

そこで言われたのが、最初の言葉だ。

柴田さん「同じ写真が2枚あると、コンテストは失格になるの。だからあなたのは消して。今ここで」

私「消しません。私が撮ったものです」

柴田さん「証拠は？ カメラに入ってるだけなら、私のカードから写しただけかもしれないじゃない」

私「そんなこと、していません」

柴田さん「初心者にサギなんか撮れるわけないの。15年やってる私でも、年に一度あるかないかよ」

声が大きくなって、班の人たちが集まってきた。

AI 시대가 오면 부동산 가치가 떨어진다?
전 정반대로 봅니다. 정확히는 서울 부동산의 가치는 더 오릅니다.

1. AI는 분산이 아니라 서울 초집중 가속화

단순 반복 일자리를 대체하고 자본과 최상위 인재의 가치를 극대화하는 즉 양극화를 가속화하는 도구입니다. 
실리콘밸리에 AI 인재가 다시 뭉치듯
한국에선 그 모든 기회와 오프라인 네트워크가 서울로 빨려 들어갑니다. (그록봇 밋업, 오픈AI Dev Day 다 서울에서 진행했죠?)
그리고 이미 외국인 넘쳐나는 일부 지방은 치안이 무너졌다고 하죠. 인구 감소와 맞물려 병원 교육 치안 인프라가 유지되는 곳은 결국 서울뿐입니다.

2. 오프라인 네트워크과 불신의 시대
 온라인엔 AI가 찍어낸 노이즈가 진짜 같은 가짜가 넘쳐납니다. 그렇기 때문에 진짜 신뢰는 오프라인 검증이 될수밖에 없죠.  그리고 AI 본고장 미국만 봐도 길하나 차이로 우범지역과 안전지대가 갈립니다. 서울 핵심지 입지는 어느정도 검증된 커뮤니티라고 할 수 있습니다. 

3. 주거는 대체 불가 필수재 & 인플레 헷징

이건 뭐 대부분 다 아시니까 스킵

4. 디지털 비용이 싸질수록 물리적 자산가치는 상승

AI는 텍스트, 코드, 이미지, 영상, 심지어 연구까지 빠른 속도로 무한 복제합니다. 디지털 영역에서 무언가를 하나 더 만들어내는 비용이 사실상 0에 수렴하는 게 되는 거죠. 그리고 그 공급이 무한대에 가까워지면 그 자체의 희소성은 떨어집니다.
그렇기 때문에 AI로 복사가 불가능한 물리적 가치를 가진 자산의 프리미엄은 오히려 더 비싸질거라 봅니다.

물론 국가 경제 입장에선 부동산 쏠림이 줄고 주식시장이 활성화되는게 맞죠. 저도 동의합니다.

근데 반도체 호황이라는 역대급 기회조차 살리지 못하고 코스피 코스닥 단타 도박장으로 전락하는 걸 보면 한국 자본시장의 체질 개선은 향후 몇십 년은 글렀습니다 ㅋㅋ 

개인은 국가 경제의 당위를 생각하기 보다는 눈앞의 현실에 맞춰 자산을 지켜야 합니다.

8. Do Humanoid Robots (AI) Have Consciousness?

Finally, this is a question that kept coming to mind during my experience…

When we interact with IRON, do we see it as a robot or as a person?

When it can communicate naturally, observe our facial expressions, respond to our gestures and even display what appears to be emotion, how does our perception of it change?

When we start to identify with what it says, or even develop an emotional connection through interaction, will we still constantly think of it as just a humanoid robot?

What exactly is human consciousness? And to what extent can we actually prove that we ourselves are conscious?

2126657891600089302.author: CyberRobooo
2126657891600089302.name: CyberRobo
2126657891600089302.text:
7/Room for Growth: Learning About Human Society

Of all the areas discussed above, I think IRON’s greatest opportunity for growth lies in understanding human society.

Human communication goes far beyond literal words.

A sentence can carry hints, emotions, cultural conventions and complex social intentions. A glance, a gesture or even a moment of silence can communicate a great deal.

Robots will gradually need to learn how to interpret these non-verbal signals and understand the intentions behind them.

IRON can already handle basic everyday conversations and deliver explanations to groups of people.

But if it is to work in real-world sales environments, understand customer needs, gauge their interests, respond to hesitation and questions, and eventually help close a sale, it will need a much deeper understanding of human behavior, social culture and interpersonal interactions.

This may be considerably more complicated than simply improving its language capabilities.

Future humanoid robots will need to learn not just human skills, but human society itself.

2126657886898246073.author: CyberRobooo
2126657886898246073.name: CyberRobo
2126657886898246073.text:
6. Potential in Commercial Sales

From what I experienced, IRON already has some basic capabilities that could support commercial sales.

It can generally recognize and describe objects in front of it, and provide explanations about weather, everyday topics and products.

If deployed in car dealerships, shopping malls or supermarkets, these capabilities could already support basic customer guidance, product introductions and explanations.

However, understanding the multiple layers of intent behind human gestures remains a challenge.

For example, in the video, a Lady asks IRON how many fingers she is showing. But the gesture may mean more than simply asking it to count two fingers. It could also be a way of indicating the number six or making a phone-call gesture.

What the robot needs to understand is the context and intention behind the gesture, not just the gesture itself.

There is a significant difference between the two.

방금 귀국한자의 도쿄, 요코하마 3박4일 후기

1. 물가
생맥주 6~7천 원대. 체감상 한국이랑 거의 비슷함. 유니클로랑 무지도 정가는 애매하고, 할인 + 면세까지 알뜰하게 받아야 비로소 살 만함. 더이상 싸다는 느낌은 없지만, 그렇다고 비싸다도 아님. 같은 가격이면 무조건 일본 올것같음.

2. 교통비
여전히 제일 체감이 되는 부분.. 달랑 3정거장 가는데 1700원씩 빠져나감. 갈아탈 때마다 서울 통합 환승제 만든 MB 리스펙..

3. 음식
물가랑 교통비 욕하다가도 밥 한 끼 먹으면 바로 다 용서됨. 회전초밥, 야끼니꾸, 오뎅바, 라멘까지 단 한 끼도 실패 없었음.

4. 운전 매너
우회전하려는 차 있어서 멈췄더니, 운전자가 꾸벅 인사까지 박고 지나가심. ???? 충격받음
한국에선 못 볼 장면이라 은근히 제일 기억에 남음. 일단 보행자 배려인게 느껴짐. 차도 느릿느릿 가서 저럴거면 그냥 자전거가 빠르겠다 싶음. 그래서 자전거 많이 타나..?

5. 귀여운게 너무 많다
귀여운 소품들이 정말 많음. 내가봐도 사고싶어짐.. 와이프 충동구매 말리느라 힘들었음.

6. 요코하마 좋다.
여긴 생각보다 한국 사람이 거의 안보였음. 음식점 웨이팅도 안했고 분위기도 한적해서 좋았음. 그리고 도로 바로 옆에 있는 롤러코스터 같은 것도 한번 타봤는데 꿀잼 ㅋㅋㅋ 와이프가 요코하마를 더 좋아하셨음.

비싸졌어도 결국 음식이랑 매너 때문에 또 가게 될 듯. 일본은 10번 넘게 가봤는데, 최근에는 소도시만 갔었다가 이번에 도쿄가니까 새삼 그 화려함과 정돈됨에 놀람.

+ 글카도 비싸서 못샀음 ㅠㅠ

Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have reported 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths, meaning nearly half of those confirmed infected have died. Declared in May, it is already the country's deadliest Ebola epidemic and has been described by health officials as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history.

The crisis is driven by the Bundibugyo virus, a rare species of Ebola for which there is currently no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral treatment. Because vaccines and therapies developed for other Ebola species cannot simply be assumed to protect against Bundibugyo, researchers are actively investigating potential options, including clinical trials of the Ervebo vaccine, though its effectiveness against this strain remains under study.

At the same time, ongoing armed conflict is severely complicating containment efforts. Clashes between armed groups and the military have forced some emergency responders to evacuate, cut off access to affected communities, and disrupted the monitoring of people exposed to the virus. Treatment centers have also been left short-staffed. These interruptions directly threaten the core measures needed to break chains of transmission: rapidly identifying cases, delivering medical care, tracing contacts, and conducting safe burials.

Ebola spreads through direct contact with infected blood or other bodily fluids, including those of people who have died from the disease, as well as through contaminated materials. While there is no approved drug specific to the Bundibugyo strain, doctors can still save lives through early supportive care, including intravenous fluids, electrolyte replacement, and prompt treatment of complications.

The most urgent challenge now is delivering that supportive care to patients while keeping health workers and communities safe, as every disruption makes it harder to detect new infections before the virus spreads further.

A human skeleton discovered in Mexico has been dated to between 12,937 and 13,145 years ago, placing him among the earliest known inhabitants of the Americas.

In late 2021, archaeologists from Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) were excavating mammoth fossils during the construction of the Felipe Ángeles International Airport north of Mexico City. Alongside the remains of roughly 700 mammoths, 200 prehistoric camels, and 100 ancient horses, the team uncovered approximately 80% of a remarkably preserved human skeleton.

Researchers named the individual Yotzin, the Nahuatl word for "unique," because his physical features differ distinctly from the 22 other ancient skeletons previously found in the Valley of Mexico. Standing around 5 feet 9 inches tall, unusually tall for that era, he died between the ages of 25 and 30. Radiocarbon dating performed on a tooth sent to the University of Liège in Belgium recently placed his age at between 12,937 and 13,145 years old.

To trace where Yotzin's ancestors originated, scientists plan to sequence his complete genome in Spain in early 2027. Lead researcher Jorge Arturo Talavera suspects the young man was a hunter, and the discovery of a mammoth skeleton roughly 26 feet away has raised the possibility that an encounter with one of the giant animals may have cost him his life.

Still, the mammoth hypothesis remains speculative, and the full dating analysis has not yet been published in a peer-reviewed scientific journal. Talavera also emphasizes that the goal is not simply to claim a record for the oldest skeleton, but to understand who Yotzin was—a question his upcoming DNA results could finally answer.

[Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) Press Release, "INAH confirma antigüedad de 'Yotzin', esqueleto humano de hace 13,000 años hallado en el AIFA" (November 20, 2026); Martínez, A. Two white native-born North Koreans, James Dresnok Jr. and Ted Dresnok, are the sons of James Dresnok Sr., a US soldier who deserted to North Korea in 1962.

James Joseph Dresnok was a 21-year-old U.S. Army private who walked across the heavily mined Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) into North Korea in August 1962 to escape a court-martial and personal troubles. He lived in the country for over 50 years as a teacher, translator, and propaganda film actor until his death in November 2016. 

In 1979, Dresnok Sr. married Doina Bumbea, a Romanian artist who had been abducted by North Korean agents in 1978, reportedly to provide foreign defectors with non-Korean wives. She gave birth to Ted and James Jr. in the early 1980s and died of lung cancer in Pyongyang in 1997 without ever returning to Romania.

Despite their European ancestry, both brothers grew up completely immersed in North Korean society. They speak Korean as their native tongue with Pyongyang accents and speak English with heavy Korean accents. Both are married with families of their own in North Korea.
